piece.caption: Stop wasting hours tracking raw material market prices manually every single day. Using Grok's live X access integrated with Zapier, you can automate real-time price alerts directly to your WhatsApp or email. This helps you keep a pulse on commodity prices like steel and cement without the manual grind of calling suppliers or browsing news sites constantly. Zapier manages the connections securely so Grok never handles your API keys or passwords. Start by connecting Zapier within the Grok chat interface and running the setup command. Focus your energy on your site work or shop operations, not data entry. Comment PRICE for the step-by-step automation guide.

[61] Zapier Blog — Grok automation: How to use the Zapier Grok integration (Grok 4.7, Grok Bot, and more)
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-grok
Grok has a very specific edge over other AI models: live access to X, so your agents can keep their finger on the pulse a little more easily. But outside of that, Grok models and agents are still solid alternatives to what OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have on offer. And if you're using Grok for work, you'll want to connect it to the rest of your tech stack. The most secure and easiest way to do that is with Zapier.
There are two main ways to automate Grok with Zapier. First, you can add Zapier to Grok Chat, Grok Bot, or Grok Build and ask your AI assistant to act across 9,000+ apps without leaving the chat—or build automations that keep running after the chat is closed. Second, you can add Grok to the workflows you already run in Zapier, so it does research, analyzes inputs, or makes images whenever something happens in your other apps.
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 9,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Build and automate workflows from Grok (Zapier MCP)
Add Grok to your existing workflows (Grok integration)
Build and automate workflows from Grok with Zapier MCP
Add Zapier to Grok Chat, Grok Bot , or Grok Build, and Grok can reach 9,000+ apps. Connect it once, pick the apps and actions you want it to use, and it works across your stack straight from the chat. Zapier manages the logins, so Grok never handles your API keys.
Setup happens inside Grok. You don't need to create anything on Zapier's side first. You can prompt Grok to "connect Zapier," or take the following steps:
Click the Connect apps button at the bottom left. (It might say Plugins depending on which app you're in.)
Click to add the connector, log in to Zapier, and authorize Grok (it might say Cursor).
Go into a chat and run /zapier-setup to discover and connect available actions.
Once connected, you can use all the actions Zapier has available for a given app, along with the Zaps you already have configured. You can ask Grok to do things like:
"Find my last five HubSpot deals, calculate weighted pipeline, and post a summary to Slack."
"Check what's trending on X about our product launch and add the top three themes to my Notion content calendar."
"Every Monday morning, send my open Asana tasks to the team Slack channel."
The X example is a good one to try first, since Grok's real-time access to X is its most standout feature. And Zapier gives you an easy way to send that social listening somewhere useful.
Each successful action draws from your existing Zapier task allowance, the same one your Zaps already use, so your Zapier bill stays simple and straightforward. And because Zapier manages the credentials, Grok never has to ask you for an API key or password. It holds a single authorization token, so it gets access to your apps, not your keys.
One-off requests are only the start. When you catch yourself asking Grok for the same thing again and again, ask it to build a Zap instead: "When a new lead lands in Salesforce, research the company and post a three-sentence summary in #sales." Grok drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier, where it starts on real events rather than waiting for you to ask.
A few things keep it dependable over time:
The same result every run. Routine steps stay as plain automation, and Grok is brought in only where a step needs judgment, so you aren't paying for tokens on simple jobs.
Problems get a fix. Zapier logs every run. If one fails, it finds the problem and proposes a fix; you can approve it or talk it through with Grok.
Leaner over time. If a Grok step turns out to do the same thing on every run, Zapier can offer to swap it for a regular step: same output, fewer tokens.
Add Grok to your existing workflows (Grok integration)
Zapier is built for workflows that need to run the same way every time, but some of them benefit from reasoning somewhere along the line. Zapier's Grok integration lets you drop a Grok step into any Zap, right where it's useful.
You don't want an AI model running every step—that's a recipe for token burn . Moving a form submission into your CRM, for example, doesn't need reasoning, so it's a job for deterministic automation. Researching the company behind that submission, drafting an outline from a one-line brief, or spotting what's trending on social media, on the other hand, are the kinds of tasks where Grok shines.
Here's an example. Say a new lead lands in Salesforce. A Zap picks it up, sends the company name to Grok with a prompt like "Find recent news and industry challenges for this company and summarize them in three sentences," then writes the summary back to the lead record so your rep sees it before the first call. Grok only runs when there's a new lead to research, and everything around it behaves the same way each time. Because the Zap starts when the lead arrives, it keeps working with your laptop closed.
Beyond asking Grok, you can also do things like categorizing text, extracting data, and generating images.
You connect your own SpaceXSI account with an API key, so Grok usage is billed by SpaceXSI on top of the Zapier tasks your Zap uses. If you'd rather use a model that's built into Zapier, with no separate account or token billing, check out which models are available through AI by Zapier .
Here are a few ways you might bring Grok into your Zapier workflows:
Enrich new leads. When a lead is added to your CRM or submitted through a form, have Grok research the company and log recent announcements and industry challenges. Try the Salesforce version .
Turn briefs into outlines or first drafts. When a new record lands in Airtable, Asana, or Notion, send the brief to Grok and have the outline land in a Google Doc, a Notion page, or your team's Slack channel for review.
Track trending topics. Schedule a Zap to ask Grok what's trending on a topic you care about every hour, day, or week, then send the results to Slack, Gmail, or a spreadsheet you can mine for content ideas. Try the daily Slack version .
Generate images from a spreadsheet. Write prompts in Trello cards, Airtable records, or Google Sheets rows, and have Grok create the image and attach it right back to where the prompt came from. This can be handy for webinar slides and social posts when a stock photo won't cut it.
Pull data out of images. When a receipt, report screenshot, or chart is uploaded to Google Drive or QuickBooks, have Grok read it and send the key details to Slack or a Google Sheet.
Keep Grok. Zapier gives it more to work with. Zapier reaches your whole stack and your Zaps keep running after the chat ends. If one breaks, Zapier finds the problem and proposes a fix.
P rompt Grok to "connect Zapier." Or click Connect apps or Plugins and search for Zapier. Sign in to your Zapier account (or create a free one), and authorize Grok or Cursor. Then go into a chat and run /zapier-setup
